chunks: From him, from al-Abbas ibn 'Amir, from Abu al-Mu'za, from Sama'ah, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said:
"It is not appropriate for a young woman to go out to the funeral to pray over the deceased, unless she is a woman who has entered old age."

key_terms.دَخَلَتْ فِي السِّنِّ: has entered old age / advanced in years

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on young women attending funeral prayers in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* delineates the juristic preference (*istihbab*) for restricting young women's attendance at funeral processions to preserve modesty and minimize emotional distress, while exempting older women who are less prone to such trials. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on gender-specific social conduct within the broader framework of funeral rites, distinguishing between the obligation of prayer and the etiquette of attendance.
